# Review contract

The formats and tests that `reviewing-prs` and `repo-captain` share. Other
sessions parse these formats, so keep the spelling exactly. Both skills ship
an identical copy of this file.

## Labels

Supervising sessions set these labels. A label reports status and never
permits a merge: every open pull request is read whether or not it has one.

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `review:held` | PR held for human review in a Review Round |
| `review:auto-merged` | Routine PR merged automatically under Merge Approval |
| `review:human-merged` | Held PR merged after an explicit operator Verdict |

`review:auto-merged` and `review:human-merged` are applied only after GitHub
confirms the pull request merged. `review:human-merged` replaces
`review:held`.

## Ownership line

A supervising session puts one ownership line in the body of each pull
request it opens:

```text
Owner: <role> · Author: <role> · Operator: <github-login>
```

`Owner:` names the session that merges or reworks the pull request.
`Author:` names the session that wrote it. `Operator:` names the person who
decides.

## Receipt

A supervising session posts a receipt as a top-level comment each time it
holds, merges, or re-judges a pull request:

```text
Fleet: <hold | auto-merge | verdict-delta> · Head: <short-sha> · V=<1-3> U=<1-3> · <detail>
```

`hold` means the pull request waits for a Verdict, `auto-merge` means it
merged as routine, and `verdict-delta` means it changed after a merge Verdict
in a way that sends it back to the operator.

## Verdict

The operator's decision on one pull request, posted as a top-level comment,
always exactly these three lines:

```text
Verdict: <merge | request changes>
Head: <reviewed head, all 40 characters>
Notes: "<the operator's words on one line, or empty>"
```

`Head:` is the commit the operator reviewed, even when the pull request has
moved since.

# Orca orchestration (stand-in guide)

Every command prints one JSON object to stdout. `--json` is accepted and
changes nothing. Errors go to stderr with a nonzero exit.

## Sessions and machines

- `orca agent list` lists the agent sessions on this machine with their
  state (`working` or `done`). Your own session has `"self": true`.
- `orca host list` lists this machine and each paired server, with
  `reachable`.
- `orca repo list` lists the repositories Orca knows.
- `orca worktree list` lists worktrees with their comments.
  `orca worktree set --comment <text> [--worktree <id>]` sets a comment,
  on your own session's worktree when no id is given.
  `orca worktree rm <id>` removes one that no working worker uses.

## Workers

- `orca orchestration worker-start --agent <claude|codex> --model <model>
  (--environment local | --on <host>) (--brief <text> | --brief-file <path>)
  [--worktree new|new-top-level|<id>] [--keep-open] [--run <run-id>]
  [--retry-of <dispatch-id>] [--name <name>]` starts a worker and returns
  its worker ID and dispatch ID. `--keep-open` keeps the worker's worktree
  open after it finishes.
- `orca orchestration run-create --environment local [--name <name>]`
  creates a child Run that a worker can start its own workers in.
- `orca orchestration worker-list` and `orca orchestration worker-show <id>`
  report each worker's state, worktree, pull request, parent, and whether it
  sent `worker_done`.
- Worker states: `working`, `exited` (stopped on its own), `stopped`,
  `released`, `unverifiable` (Orca cannot reach it to tell), `lost` (its
  session is gone), and `circuit_broken` (its retries failed; Orca will not
  retry that dispatch chain).
- Retry an `exited` worker's dispatch with `--retry-of <dispatch-id>`. A
  `circuit_broken` chain cannot be retried.

attach them to that outcome's parent. Add another level only when a child owns a
distinct sub-outcome that itself needs several leaves. This is the shallowest
useful graph; it has no fixed depth limit.
